Resolves #18060

Related: #8868 (the one-level unmount pass this generalizes), neomjs/neo-agent-institution#76 (the consumer: the fleet roster's empty rows after a settled-empty refill), neomjs/neo-agent-institution#74

`syncVnodeTree` told only the receiver's direct children that their nodes left. A child whose update merged into a covering ancestor flight (`updateDepth: -1`, or any depth greater than its distance) has its payload dropped by the collision filter, never receives a vnode, and never ran the unmount pass for ITS removed children — they kept `mounted: true` and a stale vnode, so every later re-seat by reference sent a placeholder for a node the DOM no longer had. The pass is now a mixin method, `unmountRemovedChildren(vnodeMap, presentSet)`: `syncVnodeTree` calls it for the receiver and for every component pass 1 synced, and a removed child runs the same test on its own children. Presence is tested at every level — pass 1 found it, or its root node is in the synced tree's node map — so a pruned branch (the worker keeps its previous subtree) and a node MOVED out of a removed parent in the same update (the worker emits `removeNode` after every `moveNode` for exactly that reuse) both keep their vnode and their `mounted` flag. `mounted` records state; the DOM operation already happened.

Evidence: L3 (unit-project execution at the head; red-first in worktrees at `origin/dev@8c86f4478f` and at this PR's previous head `36bf90cb93`; the browser fixture driven in Chromium; the consumer's journey green on a locally patched install) → L3 required (every AC on #18060 is unit- or component-reachable; the institution row is post-merge by construction). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#76.

## Deltas from ticket

- **A mixin method, not module-level functions** (operator review, 2026-09-02): the first head put the helpers beside the class as module functions — an unoverridable seam in an engine built for extension. `unmountRemovedChildren` is a `VdomLifecycle` method now (every component carries it through `component.Abstract`), and the profile spec exercises the seam by restating the pre-extension pass as class overrides.
- **Presence tested at every level, not a blind subtree walk** (operator review): `vdom.Helper#update` concatenates `removeNode` deltas after every other delta so a child of a removed node can be moved elsewhere in the same batch; the previous head's recursion unmounted such a moved descendant. The move arm builds exactly that update, asserts the worker's `moveNode` precedes the `removeNode`, and is red at `36bf90cb93` (1 failed / 4 passed) and green here.
- **for-loops in the hot path** (operator review): no `forEach` in the pass, and the cheapest test (`presentSet.has`) runs first, so a present child costs one Set lookup.
- **Benchmark with and without the change** (operator review): `test/playwright/unit/vdom/SyncVnodeTreeProfile.spec.mjs` — 200 rows × 5 leaves (1,200 components), the extended pass against the one-level pass on the same worker output, interleaved after a warm-up, medians of 30 samples. Three quiet-machine runs at the head, every child present: 6.11 / 6.28 / 6.25 ms vs 5.42 / 5.50 / 5.84 ms (ratios 1.13 · 1.14 · 1.07); half the rows removed: 3.94 / 4.16 / 4.15 ms vs 2.75 / 2.97 / 3.02 ms (ratios 1.43 · 1.40 · 1.37). On `dev`, where both classes run the same one-level algorithm, the ratio reads 1.03 — the measurement floor. The bounds asserted in CI are 2× and 3×.
- **Component-based test** (operator review): `test/playwright/component/container/PooledChildUnmount.spec.mjs` on a new `apps/pooled-children` fixture — the same scenario through the real workers and the real DOM, 3 arms green here; at `origin/dev` all three are red, including the pool-alone CONTROL: the nested component's stale vnode makes the refill render no row at all in a real browser, a fact the unit control (which asserts the cards, not their children) cannot see.

## Evolution

The first head widened the pass by recursing blindly through a removed component's logical subtree. The operator's review named the case that breaks: the worker orders `removeNode` last so a node inside a removed node can be moved out in the same update, and a blind walk unmounts it. The rework tests presence at every level instead, moves the pass onto the mixin so a class can narrow or skip it, and measures the cost against the pass it replaced.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #18060 (the full body, including the Architectural Reality and Avoided Traps sections), the changed-file list, `origin/dev`'s `syncVnodeTree` (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs` L905–978), `ComponentManager.getChildren` / `getDirectChildren` / `childMap` maintenance (`src/manager/Component.mjs` L246–299, L510–599), `VNodeUtil.createMap` / `getChildIds` / `getVnode` (`src/util/VNode.mjs` L24–47, L190–219), the #8868 sibling precedent (`test/playwright/unit/vdom/HiddenChildren.spec.mjs`), the unit run policy (`test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs`) and the workflow that consumes it (`.github/workflows/test.yml` L222–313). The PR body was read as a claim set to check, not as the premise.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The unmount pass must cover exactly the set that pass 1 mounts silently — the components whose `_vnode` is written without `afterSetVnode` firing, so their own `syncVnodeTree` never runs — and must recurse into the removed subtree, because a re-inlined parent references its children by id. It must NOT hardcode a depth (one level, two levels, "children of `me`"): the correct boundary is "whatever the new vnode carries", derived from pass 1's own membership. It must not re-crawl the vnode per component, must not touch pass 1's membership (the 2026-03 `getChildComponents` swap is a known regression), and must keep the placeholder-vs-removal distinction rather than treating map-absence as removal unconditionally. Test isolation: a red-first spec beside `HiddenChildren.spec.mjs` with the merged-flight arm separated from the consequence arm, so a partial fix names itself.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Matches**, and on the one axis I expected to have to argue about it is right for a reason the PR body understates. The "at every depth" claim in the title is load-bearing and I did not take it on trust: it holds only because `ComponentManager.getChildren` delegates to `VNodeUtil.getChildIds`, which recurses through the whole tree (`src/util/VNode.mjs:196`) while skipping `componentId` placeholders. So `childComponents` really is every component the new vnode carries in full, and reusing `childComponentsSet` as the present-set for a descendant's children is sound rather than coincidental. Two other things I checked and expected to flag: dropping the old `if (me.vnode)` guard around the map lookup is behaviour-identical, because `createMap(null)` returns an empty `Map` (`getVnode` passes `null` through, the `if (vnode)` body is skipped); and `vnodeMap` is built once, before any unmount runs, so `unmountSubtree` nulling a `_vnode` cannot poison a later placeholder resolution in the same pass.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert and with friction → gold. The friction was a product symptom in another repo (institution #76's empty rows); rather than absorbing it app-side — three shapes were tried there and each is written down with why it failed — it was converted into an engine invariant with a reproducer that outlives the incident. The Avoided Traps section is the visible form of that: the 2026-03 attempt is cited as a rejected shape, not rediscovered.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the focus-revert cascade is a new, unexercised consequence of recursing.**

`unmountSubtree` writes `mounted = false` through the public config, so every descendant of a removed node now runs `Component#afterSetMounted(false)` → `revertFocus()` (`src/component/Base.mjs:716`, `:1778`). Before this PR those descendants never flipped at all, so at most one `revertFocus()` fired per removal; now the whole logical subtree fires, **top-down** — `unmountSubtree` unmounts the parent before recursing.

For the overwhelming majority of components that is two property reads and a return, because `revertFocus` is guarded by `this.containsFocus && relatedTarget`. The case that is not: a removal whose subtree **contained focus**. `containsFocus` is true for every ancestor in the focused chain, and each of those records its own `focusEnterData.relatedTarget`. If a nested chain recorded different relatedTargets, each level calls `Neo.getComponent(relatedTarget.id)?.focus()` in turn and the **deepest** one wins — so focus after a pooled-row removal could land somewhere other than where the outermost revert put it. Whether that materialises depends on whether the browser's own `focusout` has already cleared `containsFocus` by the time the sync runs, which is exactly the kind of ordering I cannot settle by reading.

Non-blocking: the prior behaviour (descendants silently retaining `mounted: true`) was strictly worse, and nothing here regresses a case that previously worked. But it is new surface. **Suggested empirical isolation test (guide §5.1)** rather than an argument: focus a field inside a pooled row, clear the pool inside a covering ancestor flight, and assert where `document.activeElement` / the focused component lands — once with the recursion, once with `unmountSubtree` flattened to a single level. If the two agree, the concern is dead and the spec is worth keeping as the arm that says so.

**Two falsifiers I ran that CLEARED you — both worth the record:**

1. **The `MainRenderQueue` attribution.** The body disposes of the one local red as *"a load-timing flake outside this diff; the spec does not reach `syncVnodeTree`"* — which is an inference sitting on the only checkable sentence in the run. My working hypothesis was cross-file contamination: the new spec patches the global `Neo.applyDeltas` at module scope and restores it only in `afterAll`, and `MainRenderQueue.spec.mjs` lives in the same directory. I measured the baseline first — full `npm run test-unit` at `dev@9dcafc5fa2` (my clone, no fix, no new spec): **2942 passed, 0 failed**, and `vdom/` alone **160 passed**. So "pre-existing" was not reproducing on my machine and the hypothesis was still live. It died on the mechanism: `MainRenderQueue.spec.mjs` drives its assertions through `execFile` in a **spawned Node process** (`src/Main.mjs` imported inside the child script), so the parent worker's patched `Neo.applyDeltas` cannot reach it — and a subprocess spec is precisely the shape that fails under machine load and passes 3/3 alone. Your attribution is correct, and the module-scope patch is idiomatic here (eight sibling specs in `unit/vdom/` do the identical thing with the identical comment). Withdrawn before posting.
2. **Cross-window unmounting.** The widened pass has no `windowId` guard, while `executeVdomUpdate` carries an explicit one (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:254`), so I checked whether a child living in another window could be absent from this window's vnode and get unmounted out from under it. `childMap` is keyed by `parentId` and maintained on every `parentId` change (`src/manager/Component.mjs:510–541`), and `container.Base` propagates `windowId` down its items (`src/container/Base.mjs:317`) — so a stable parent/child pair shares a window, and a mismatch is transient mid-propagation at worst. Not a finding.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: The mount and unmount halves of `syncVnodeTree` had different reach for as long as both existed — pass 1 always walked the whole vnode (`getChildIds` recurses), pass 2 always walked one level (`getDirectChildren(me.id)`) — and nothing named the asymmetry, so #8868 fixed the depth-1 case and the invariant read as complete. Worth a node: when a lifecycle method has a "do X for the tree" pass and an "undo X" pass, their **reach** is part of the contract and belongs in the JSDoc as a stated set, not left implicit in which manager method each one happens to call.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` makes a spec's real coverage invisible from its result: `grid/Teleportation.spec.mjs` reports nothing in CI, and the `unit` check goes green without it. Nothing warns an author writing an AC that names a CI-skipped spec, and nothing warns a reviewer reading "CI-covered". A cheap fix would be for the skip-guarded specs to be enumerated somewhere an AC author can see, or for the guard to emit a visible skipped-count in the CI summary.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The reusable artifact is the escalation discipline, not the diff. Three app-side fix shapes were tried in the consumer repo, each failure written down (duplicated rows mid-fade; a lost child `Image` after re-inline — which is *the recursion requirement*, discovered app-side before it was understood engine-side), and only then was the engine touched. That is what makes the recursion in step 3 evidence-backed rather than defensive: the third failed shape IS the test case for it. Ledgering failed attempts in the consumer converted three dead ends into the fix's specification.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:**

The MOVE arm asserts `expect(inner.parentId).toBe(slot.id)` — so after the flight, `inner` is **mounted, with a vnode, and its logical parent is an unmounted vnode-less component**. That is the correct call for this update (the node really did move, and re-parenting is not `syncVnodeTree`'s job), but it leaves a state worth naming: `ComponentManager.getDirectChildren(slot.id)` still returns a live mounted child under a dead parent.

Concretely, what I would want to know before this pattern spreads: if a later update passes `slot` to `unmountRemovedChildren` — it is unmounted, so pass 1 should not surface it, but `getDirectChildren` still links them — does `inner` get re-tested against a tree it is no longer positioned in? I could not construct a case where it goes wrong, and I am not asserting one exists. It is the edge I would put a spec on next, and it is cheap to pin now while the mechanism is fresh in your head.

Not blocking, and deliberately not a Required Action — the current arm is correct as written.
